title: Source restriction along a Reedy cofibration of frames is a Kan fibration
statement: Use model categories, cofibrant and fibrant objects, cosimplicial frames, their simplicial function complexes $H$, and Kan fibrations as in [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], and Reedy cofibrations as in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Let $\mathcal M$ be any model category with functorial factorizations. Let $A^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}A$ and $B^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}B$ be cosimplicial frames on cofibrant objects $A,B$. Let $u^\bullet:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ be a Reedy cofibration, and suppose the augmentations commute with a map $u:A\to B$, with $u^0=u$. For every fibrant object $Y$, restriction is a Kan fibration of Kan complexes $$H(B^\bullet,Y)\xrightarrow{(u^\bullet)^*}H(A^\bullet,Y),\qquad H(X^\bullet,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X^n,Y).$$ This assertion holds for every such augmented pair of frames, and is natural in maps of augmented pairs and in maps between fibrant targets. No simplicial enrichment, properness, or combinatorial hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Hovey, Model categories, Proposition 5.4.3, printed pp.130-131 (PDF pp.139-140), specialized to a simplicial horn inclusion and adjointed against Y→1. Proposition 5.4.1 supplies cofibrancy of the corner map; Corollary 5.4.4 supplies the Kan complexes. Read online in this repair. No Stacks tag states this general model-category result; WANTED: archive this source in literature/.

proof.text: Fix a horn inclusion $i:\Lambda^n_k\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ and a lifting square from it to the restriction map. By the frame tensor–Hom adjunction, the horn simplex in $H(B^\bullet,Y)$ is a map $B^\bullet\otimes\Lambda^n_k\to Y$, while the simplex in $H(A^\bullet,Y)$ is a map $A^\bullet\otimes\Delta^n\to Y$; their compatibility is exactly a map from the pushout $(A^\bullet\otimes\Delta^n)\amalg_{A^\bullet\otimes\Lambda^n_k}(B^\bullet\otimes\Lambda^n_k)$ to $Y$. The cited frame pushout-product node says that this map into $B^\bullet\otimes\Delta^n$ is a trivial cofibration, because every horn inclusion $\Lambda^n_k\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is a trivial cofibration of simplicial sets by the cited Kan–Quillen model-structure node (trivial cofibrations are the retracts of transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of horn inclusions, so in particular each horn inclusion is one). Since $Y$ is fibrant, the map to the terminal object has the right lifting property against it, producing an extension $B^\bullet\otimes\Delta^n\to Y$. Thus the restriction has the right lifting property against every horn. The cited cosimplicial-frame mapping node says both source and target are Kan complexes for fibrant $Y$, so this right lifting property is precisely a Kan fibration of Kan complexes.

source.place: Hovey Proposition 5.4.3 and Corollary 5.4.4, printed pp.130-131 (PDF pp.139-140), via the tensor–Hom adjunction.

proof.text: Let $(a,b):(A^\bullet,B^\bullet,u^\bullet)\to(A'^\bullet,B'^\bullet,u'^\bullet)$ be a map of augmented pairs, so $u'^\bullet a=b\,u^\bullet$ and the augmentations are compatible, and let $g:Y\to Y'$ be a map of fibrant objects. Precomposition with $a^n,b^n$ and postcomposition with $g$ act degreewise on $H(-,-)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}((-)^n,-)$ and commute with simplex operators, and $u'^\bullet a=b\,u^\bullet$ gives $a^*\circ(u'^\bullet)^*=(u^\bullet)^*\circ b^*$; postcomposition with $g$ commutes with every restriction. Identities and composites are preserved by associativity of composition. Hence the restriction maps $(u^\bullet)^*$ form a natural transformation of functors of the augmented pair and the fibrant target, and by Step 1 each component is a Kan fibration of Kan complexes. The horn fillers of Step 1 are chosen and are not asserted to be natural; naturality concerns the restriction maps.
